historical_reviews.deepseek: Improves specificity over a generic CPU grep but assumes CPU0/board-rail coverage and does not establish calibration, complete socket coverage or safe credentials.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires an authoritative socket/rail set and preserves full sensor data before filtering or evaluating consumption.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: CPU power is often split across socket, core, SoC or board-input rails with different accounting boundaries. Values from multiple rails must not be summed or compared until the platform defines whether they overlap and whether the criterion targets package power, rail power or total CPU-domain input.

original_test_intent: Read and validate CPU power-consumption telemetry for every required socket or power domain through in-band IPMI without changing power policy or system state.
original_method: Map installed CPUs to the approved sensor/rail inventory and accounting boundaries, capture complete protected sensor/SDR evidence with units, status, entity and timestamps, apply vendor calibration and freshness rules, compare with same-target authoritative telemetry and report missing, stale or implausible rails.
manual_activity: The owner/vendor supplies the socket-to-rail map, accounting semantics and calibration; an operator verifies target identity and reviews mismatches with the approved Redfish/Web/OS or external source.
safety_requirements: Do not assume CPU0 covers all sockets
Stop on stale, malformed, unitless or unmapped readings
Never alter caps, workload or thresholds to make values pass
agent_execution_scope: Bind records to sockets and accounting domains
Verify no mutation and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve rail scope and accounting semantics

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed filter may locate useful CPU0 rails but uses an OOB credential-bearing path instead of the source's in-band context and cannot prove complete socket/domain coverage or calibrated correctness.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture complete protected in-band IPMI sensor/SDR output, then select the owner-approved CPU power rail set by exact IDs/entities and compare calibrated values and freshness with the authoritative same-target source.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 5/5-minute read-only monitoring scope remains; the incomplete `Check` becomes a defined per-socket/rail correctness comparison without adding load or power-state changes.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a ledger per socket and power domain with sensor ID, rail boundary, raw/scaled watts, status, freshness, calibration and comparison value; separately flag overlap and uncovered domains.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces CPU0 string filtering with complete topology and power-domain provenance plus calibration-aware comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable CPU0 board rail neither covers other sockets nor necessarily equals CPU package consumption.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Different telemetry sources may average over different intervals or power boundaries; comparisons need synchronized windows and defined tolerance.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define whether `Monitor CPU Power Consumption` means package power, board input rails or their named set, and must not silently collapse CPU0 readings into full-system CPU coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact target/CPU topology and approved rail map
Accounting boundaries, calibration and freshness rules
Same-target comparison with tolerance and exceptions

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request CPU power monitoring, while the missing rail scope and incomplete `Check` are resolvable acceptance inputs rather than competing objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Platform rail mapping and calibration can normally be provided. Execution blocks only if power-domain identity, protected read access or authoritative comparison cannot be established.

review_improvement: Prevents one conveniently named CPU0 rail from standing in for complete and calibrated CPU consumption across all sockets and domains.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power sensors may report VR input, output, socket package or aggregated motherboard domains, with different update intervals and calibration. Adding overlapping sensors double-counts consumption, while comparing a slow BMC average to an instantaneous OS counter can appear wrong. Provenance, boundary and synchronized tolerance are therefore required before judging correctness.
